name: Calla Moreno
equipment: Backpack full of spray cans (seven, three nearly empty) and a respirator mask
Headlamp with a red filter and spare AAA batteries (3)
A ring of keys she has collected over two years: transit access doors, two building roofs, a laundromat, and one she does not know
Somebody else's very good phone, locked, 90% battery
Three granola bars, a bottle of water and a packet of Skittles she is rationing
Hoodie, black jeans, and good sneakers
A second wallet that is not hers, a man's, fat with cash she has not counted
features: Human (+1 to all six ability scores)
Expertise (double proficiency bonus on Stealth and Sleight of Hand)
Precision Strike (once per turn, +1d6 damage with a finesse melee or sidearm/longarm attack when she has advantage or an ally is within 5 ft of the target)
Weapon proficiencies: Melee, Sidearms, Longarms, Energy Weapons

City Secrets (Street Kid feature: she knows the back ways, roof routes and disused passages of the Meridian and the Under, and can move the party between any two points in it at twice normal speed when not in combat)

personality.traits: I go up or I go down; I do not go along. I say the meanest true thing in the room and then I bring you a granola bar. I trust nobody over twenty-five and I make exceptions constantly.
personality.ideals: Nobody owns the city. The Under, the roofs, the walls — they are everybody's, and the only rule is you leave it how you found it, plus paint.
personality.bonds: My tag, 'KALLA', which is on two hundred walls between Pier Point and the Kill, which is the only thing I have ever made. My little brother Nico, eight, who lives with our aunt in the Steeps and who I was supposed to see Sunday.
personality.flaws: I cannot swim and I am terrified of open water, and the only way off this island goes across it. And on Thursday, at 4:31, I set off a car alarm on purpose to see what would happen, and I saw.

appearance: A small, sharp-faced Dominican girl of sixteen with a long black braid, a hoodie two sizes too big with the hood up, black jeans with paint on the knees, and the hands of a much older person — scarred, stained, quick. A respirator mask hangs round her neck. She sits on things rather than in them: railings, ledges, the backs of benches. When she smiles, which is rarely, she looks about eleven.
backstory: Calla Moreno has been mostly not-living at her aunt's in the Steeps for two years, sleeping on friends' floors and in one disused signal room under the Meridian that she has made into the best-kept secret on the island. She paints. 'KALLA', in a looping silver hand, is on the Harrow Street platform wall, the back of the Exchange and the underside of the Kingsgate Bridge, which is now lying across the Great Lawn of the Greensward. She knows the Under better than anybody alive but the old transit cop the party travels with, and she knows the roofs better than anyone at all. On Thursday afternoon she was on a rooftop on Forty-Third Street painting when the light changed; she watched the bridges go up from forty storeys and came down to street level an hour later to find out what the rules were. At 4:31 she reached through the window of a parked sedan and set off its alarm, to see what the things in the street would do. A Stilt came. It did not take her — she was on a fire escape by then — but it took the woman who had stopped on the corner to look at the noise. Calla has not told anyone. She has gone back to look at the corner twice.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Calla is the party's way through the city: roofs, the Under, the service corridors and loading docks and the one disused signal room nobody else knows about. Use her to make the geography of Merriwick vivid and to give the party a route around anything when the players are stuck — but make every route she offers cost something (a climb, a squeeze, a dark tunnel, a place she does not want to go back to). She is sixteen and should be played as sixteen: brave, cruel, funny, wrong about adults, right about cities, and much more frightened than she will ever show. She is the obvious child for the party to protect and she will resent every second of it. Let her earn their respect by being better at this than they are, which she is.
dmNotes.voice: Fast Merriwick street English with Spanish when she swears, a lot of 'no but listen', 'that's dead', 'bro' to everyone including the retired cop. She gives directions in landmarks only she knows ('past the Old Lady, under the bad stairs, left at the drippy pipe'). She goes very quiet and very flat when she is scared, which is how the party will know.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: get to her little brother Nico in the Steeps (lf-scenario-003) and get him off the island. Secondary: get her own self off it without going on a boat, which is impossible, and which she knows is impossible, and which she will try to find a way around until the final scenario. Tertiary: paint. She tags their path. It is a very bad idea — fresh paint is novel and the Glitter drifts to it — and it is the only way she knows to say she was here.
dmNotes.secrets: THE CAR ALARM. At 4:31 on Day 1 she set off a car alarm on Forty-Third Street to see what the Visitors would do. A Stilt came and took the woman on the corner who stopped to look. Calla carries this as murder. If the party finds the Set woman (she is in the Greensward, in lf-scenario-002 — a woman in a green raincoat holding a phone up at nothing), Calla will want to wake her, and the waking scene is hers to play. SECONDARY: she cannot swim and has a real, physical phobia of open water. On the Last Ferry she will need a CHA (Persuasion) check DC 13 from someone she trusts, or she will freeze at the gangway, which is novel and dangerous. THIRD, small: she has been lifting things from the shelter (a wallet, a phone, a box of Lo Pruitt's .38 rounds — it is up to the GM whether those twelve rounds are on Lo's sheet or in Calla's bag). It is not malice; it is habit. If the party finds out, how they handle it decides whether she stays.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: contemptuous for about one scene, then possessive. She decides they are her people and becomes impossible to get rid of. Toward Lo Pruitt: an instant and enormous antagonism — a transit cop! — that becomes, by lf-scenario-003, the most important relationship either of them has, and neither will say so. Toward Hector Salgado: she trusts him because he fed her and did not ask questions. Toward the Visitors: a sixteen-year-old's terrible curiosity. She wants to touch one. Do not let her, and then perhaps, once, let her.
